observations: Bare V8 engine out of a vehicle, no transmission attached, placed on dark pavement.
Valve covers clearly marked 'iFORCE' and '4.7L' in photos 0 and 1, matching the Toyota 2UZ-FE 4.7L V8.
Red paint dot on intake manifold in all three photos, likely a sorting/grading mark from a Japanese auction yard.
Serpentine belt, fan clutch, and pulleys appear intact and in place in photo 2.
Wiring harness and some hoses look cut or dangling in photos 0 and 1, consistent with an engine pulled from a donor vehicle.
No oil pan, bottom end, or electrical connector close-ups shown.
No video or sound of the engine running; it is shown static and disconnected.
'WARNING' sticker visible near the alternator area in photos 0 and 1, text not fully legible.
Background shows other engines and a person standing nearby, suggesting a scrapyard/parts dealer setting.

claims.evidence: No import documentation, auction sheet, or chassis tag shown in any photo; origin cannot be confirmed from images alone.

claims.claim: Commonly found in vehicles like Toyota Tundra, Sequoia, Land[cruiser]
claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1 badge reading '4.7L iFORCE' matches the known Toyota 2UZ-FE engine used in these models.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical condition (compression, bearings, timing chain wear) cannot be seen from exterior photos.
risks.proof: A start-up video with audible idle and a compression test reading per cylinder.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not running / for-parts condition

risks.risk: Wiring harness and sensors may be incomplete or cut, raising reinstallation cost.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all harness connectors and sensor plugs.
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete harness, buyer to source missing connectors

risks.risk: Oil pan, block, and lower end could have cracks, oil leaks, or prior repair welds not visible from these angles.
risks.proof: Photos of the underside/oil pan and any visible leaks.

risks.risk: Mileage or usage history is unknown; 'fairly used' is subjective and unverifiable from a photo.
risks.proof: Odometer photo from donor vehicle or Japanese auction export certificate.

risks.risk: Red paint dot may indicate a grading mark (e.g., a flagged defect) from the auction sheet, meaning the engine could have been rejected for a specific fault.
risks.proof: Auction inspection sheet or grading certificate photo.
risks.if_unproven: priced as flagged/defective until the grading sheet is shown

proof_requests: Start-up video with sound showing the engine running or turning over.
Photo of the underside/oil pan area.
Close-up of wiring harness connectors and sensors.
Any Japanese auction sheet, export certificate, or chassis plate confirming origin and mileage.
response.reason: The engine is clearly identifiable as a Toyota 2UZ-FE 4.7L iFORCE V8 from the readable valve cover badge, but with no running video or internal condition evidence it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, non-running used engine.
